interactive.title: Black hole
interactive.text: A black hole is a region of spacetime exhibiting such strong gravitational effects that nothing—including particles and electromagnetic radiation such as light—can escape from inside it. The theory of general relativity predicts that a sufficiently compact mass can deform spacetime to form a black hole. The boundary of the region from which no escape is possible is called the event horizon. Although crossing the event horizon has enormous effect on the fate of the object crossing it, it appears to have no locally detectable features. In many ways a black hole acts like an ideal black body, as it reflects no light. Moreover, quantum field theory in curved spacetime predicts that event horizons emit Hawking radiation, with the same spectrum as a black body of a temperature inversely proportional to its mass. This temperature is on the order of billionths of a kelvin for black holes of stellar mass, making it essentially impossible to observe.

blanks.why: 'Strong' describes powerful effects such as gravity; 'strongly' is an adverb and cannot describe a noun.
After 'can' we need a base verb, and 'escape from inside' means to get out.
General relativity is a scientific theory, and 'The ... of general relativity predicts' needs a noun.
'Predicts that' introduces the full clause saying what the theory predicts.
The subject 'The boundary' is singular, so it needs 'is called'.
'Although' shows the contrast between an enormous effect and having no detectable features.
'Have an effect on' uses the noun 'effect'; 'affect' is a verb.
'It appears to have' means 'it seems to have'; an object cannot refuse, forget or pretend.

distractors: The Milky Way's central black hole, known as Sagittarius A*, has a mass four million times greater than the Sun.
Dark matter is transparent to electromagnetic radiation and/or is so dense and small that it fails to absorb or emit enough radiation to be detectable with current imaging technology.
It is the speed of all massless particles such as photons, and associated fields—including electromagnetic radiation such as light—in a vacuum.
missing.why: It introduces the idea of a 'black body', which the next sentence continues with 'Moreover' and 'the same spectrum as a black body'.

highlights.question: What does the theory of general relativity say a dense enough mass can do?
How low is the temperature of a black hole with the mass of a star?

distractors: Most of the mass in the universe is made of an invisible kind of matter.
The center of our galaxy holds a black hole millions of times heavier than the Sun.
The radiation from a black hole is hot enough to be observed easily from Earth.
idea.why: The first sentence says that nothing, including light, can escape because the gravitational effects are so strong.

titles.why: Every sentence is about black holes: how they form, their event horizon and their radiation.

interactive.title: What Is the Key to Success? And How Do We Get There?
interactive.text: Better at spelling! In one study, 12-year-old kids who were competing in a national spelling bee were given a series of questionnaires to fill out—including a grit questionnaire. Interestingly, it was not the kids who read books for fun or those who were quizzed on spelling words by their parents who ended up doing better in the spelling bee. Instead, it was the kids who scored high on grit who made it to the final round of the national spelling bee. What's more, gritty high school students are more likely to graduate, and university students get higher grades. In adulthood, gritty employees are more likely to be keeping their jobs and their marriages! What about the brains of these highly successful, gritty people—what do their brains look like? And furthermore, are the brains of gritty people different from those of not-so-gritty, less successful individuals?

'Were competing in' needs the -ing verb; people compete in a contest such as a spelling bee.
'Read books for fun' is a fixed expression meaning for enjoyment.
'Those who' refers to people and is the subject of 'were quizzed'.
A possessive word is needed before the noun 'parents'.
'Instead' gives the opposite of the sentence before: not those kids, but the gritty ones.
You 'score high' on a questionnaire, and the past tense matches the rest of the story.
'The final round' is the last stage of a competition; an adjective is needed before 'round'.

distractors: This number has increased consistently since it was first tracked at the national level in 2011.
Males and females achieved at roughly similar levels.
Peer groups are important to adolescents in a new way, as they begin to develop an identity separate from their parents and exert independence.

interactive.title: Twenty Tips for High-School Students Engaging in Research with Scientists
interactive.text:
For our first research experience, we wanted to ask a question that could contribute to the improvement of education for future generations. If school architects understood the current research about the influences of color on the brain and learning, it could benefit their designs. Our question focused on our own environment, in hopes that our work could have an impact. These questions may leave you wondering whether our school looks like a painting by Miro – but while gray on the outside, the interior is actually quite colorful. Our personal interactions with color in our environment inspired us to ask more.

Look for background information by exploring the field of research you will be working in and by reading available publications. Ask for guidance from scientists, in particular, about accessing the relevant scientific literature. Indeed, our lack of expertise in the field made it easy to get lost digging into issues of little relevance. Consider reading a few research articles to start. Though it may not be easy, the concepts are much more accessible if you read them step by step.

blanks.why: 'Wanted to' is followed by a base verb, and we say 'ask a question'.
'Contribute to' means to help bring about something, here the improvement of education.
'If ... it could' makes a conditional sentence about a possible benefit.
After 'could' we need a verb; the research 'could benefit' (help) their designs.
'In hopes that' is followed by a full clause.
'Wondering whether' introduces a yes/no question; 'weather' means rain, sun and wind.
'On the outside' contrasts with 'the interior' later in the sentence.
'Inspired us to ask' means it gave us the wish to ask; a past-tense verb fits.

distractors: The question should also be broad enough to have universal merit.
Field research refers to gathering primary data from a natural environment.
This question is extremely important to brain researchers all over the world.
missing.why: The next sentence ('Indeed, our lack of expertise...') explains why students need guidance from scientists.

highlights.question: What topic of research did the students think could help school architects?
Why did the students sometimes waste time on issues that did not matter much?

idea.answer: The students' research question was about how color in their surroundings affects learning.
distractors: The students' school is brightly colored outside but plain gray inside.
Watching a movie affects the brain in the same way as reading a book.
A research question should be narrow enough to study in one place and time.
idea.why: The students say their question focused on their own environment and on how color influences the brain and learning.

distractors: How Do Bees Find Their Way Home?

interactive.title: Smelting
interactive.text:
Iron is smelted from iron ore in large reactors called blast furnaces. A blast furnace is a tall vertical structure which is fed with coke, iron ore and limestone. When hot air is blown in the blast furnace, the coke will burn and reduce the oxygen off the ore, producing bare iron and carbon dioxide. The limestone will bind off any remaining bedrock. The iron melts in the hot temperature and is tapped off in liquid phase at the bottom. It is then worked into steel. The limestone and bedrock form a compound called slag. It can be used for making bricks, concrete or road topping. Earlier methods include Bloomery.

Aluminum is smelted in electric ovens called electric arc furnaces. The aluminum ore is poured on the bottom of the furnace and electric current is led through the ore. The temperature rises so high that the oxygen separates, leaving metallic aluminum.

blanks.why: A metal is smelted 'from' its ore, the rock it comes out of.
'Called' (named) introduces the name of the reactors.
'Which' begins a relative clause about a thing, the structure.
The passive 'is blown' needs the past participle; air is blown into the furnace.
The -ing form adds the result of the burning: producing iron and carbon dioxide.
Before the base verb 'bind' we need a modal verb such as 'will'.
Iron becomes liquid at a high temperature, and the singular subject needs 'melts'.
'At the bottom' is the fixed phrase for the lowest part of the furnace.

distractors: Some processes in modern technology, such as iron smelting, still produce carbon monoxide as a byproduct.
Steelmaking has existed for millennia, but it was not commercialized until the 19th century.
The ancient craft process of steelmaking was the crucible process.
missing.why: The next sentence says 'It can be used for making bricks', and 'it' must be slag, which only this sentence introduces.

highlights.question: What three materials are put into a blast furnace?
Where does the smelting of aluminum take place?

idea.answer: Iron and aluminum are both smelted from ore, but in different kinds of furnaces.
distractors: Steel is made by adding metals such as nickel and chromium to iron.
Slag is a waste product that cannot be used for anything.
Aluminum is smelted in blast furnaces that burn coke and limestone.
idea.why: Iron is smelted in blast furnaces, while aluminum is smelted in electric arc furnaces.

interactive.title: How Do Birds Cope with Losing Members of Their Group?
interactive.text: Have you ever wondered how animals might respond to losing a member of their group? Many human activities, like hunting or changing the environment animals live in, can cause the loss of individual animals. However, how this loss affects the remaining animals in a group is still widely unknown. We wanted to investigate this question, so we tracked wild birds known as great tits. These birds form small groups within their population, called flocks. By removing individual birds from the wild, we were able to monitor how birds responded to losing a flockmate. Interestingly, the birds that lost their flockmates responded by making new flockmates and also by spending more time with their previous flockmates. These findings show us that losing animals from a population can affect how the remaining animals behave. This research could help improve people's understanding of the effects of losing animals.

blanks.why: 'Have you ever ...' needs a past participle, and 'wondered' means asked yourself.
'A member of their group' is one animal that belongs to the group.
'Like' here means 'such as' and introduces examples of human activities.
After 'can' we need a base verb; hunting can cause the loss of animals.
'Affects' is the verb meaning 'has an influence on'; 'effects' is usually a noun.
'Wanted to' needs a base verb, and scientists investigate (study) a question.
'So' shows the result: they wanted to study the question, so they tracked birds.
The small groups are inside, or within, the larger population.

distractors: Paired birds often stay close to each other during the day no matter what they are doing, for example feeding or resting.
Furthermore, graylag geese have strong family bonds and goslings stay close to their parents until the next breeding season.
Spending time with friends has been shown to cause more activity in the parts of the brain that makes us feel good – the reward circuits.
missing.why: It reports how the birds responded, which the next sentence calls 'these findings'.

highlights.question: What are two human activities that can lead to the loss of animals?
What do the findings show that the loss of animals can change?

idea.answer: Birds that lost flockmates made new ones and spent more time with their old ones.
distractors: Birds that lost flockmates stayed alone and avoided the rest of the flock.
Great tits live alone and do not form groups with other birds.
Many birds help people by spreading the seeds of important plants.
idea.why: The passage says the birds responded by making new flockmates and spending more time with previous flockmates.

titles.answer: How Do Birds Cope with Losing Members of Their Group?
distractors: How Having a Partner and a Family Changes the Stress Levels of Graylag Geese
Why Didn’t the Bird Cross the Road?
titles.why: The whole passage is about a study of how birds respond when members of their group are lost.

interactive.title: Holidays With Grandmother
interactive.text: Odongo and Apiyo were excited because it was time to visit their grandmother again. They packed their bags and got ready for their long journey the next day. They could not sleep and talked about the holiday the whole night. Early the next morning, they left for the village in their father's car. They drove past mountains, wild animals, and tea plantations. They counted cars and sang songs. After a while, the children were tired and fell asleep. Father woke up Odongo and Apiyo as they arrived in the village. They found Nyar-Kanyada, their grandmother, resting on a mat under a tree. In their language, Nyar-Kanyada means "daughter of the people of Kanyada." She was a strong and beautiful woman. Nyar-Kanyada welcomed them into the house. She danced around the room singing with joy. Her grandchildren were excited to give her the presents they brought from the city.

blanks.why: People feel 'excited' (-ed adjective) about something good, like a visit.
'Time to' is followed by a base verb, and you visit a relative.
You 'pack your bags' before a trip, and the story is in the past tense.
We 'talk about' a topic.
'Leave for' a place means to start a journey to it.
'Drove past' uses the preposition 'past'; 'passed' is a verb.
'Sang' is the simple past of 'sing', like 'counted'.
'Fell asleep' is the past tense of 'fall asleep'.

distractors: She left to go to her grandmother's manyatta, but she got lost in the hills.
One day, three sisters, Apiyo, Ajoh and Atieno went to the forest to fetch firewood.
While they were standing in the garden, Thabo arrived.
missing.why: The children had fallen asleep, so they had to be woken up when they arrived, before 'they found' their grandmother.

highlights.question: What did the children see on the way to the village?
What was the grandmother doing when the children found her?

idea.answer: The children were very happy to travel to the village to see their grandmother.
distractors: The children traveled to the village by bus with their mother.
Grandmother was too tired to welcome the children into her house.
Grandmother told the children stories about the snakes in the forest.
idea.why: They were excited to visit, could not sleep the night before, and brought her presents.

distractors: My first day at the market
titles.why: The story is about the children's holiday trip to visit their grandmother.

interactive.title: Hyena, Hare and their basins
interactive.text:
Long time ago, Hyena and Hare were great friends. They were both poor but Hare owned a donkey. He also had a very small basin, which he used to feed the donkey.

One hot afternoon, Hare decided to give water to his donkey.

However, Hare could not fetch water from the well with his small basin. So he decided to borrow a bigger basin from Hyena. Hyena gave Hare his basin because of their friendship.

After getting water and giving it to the donkey, Hare went home with Hyena's basin.

Two weeks later, Hyena wanted to wash clothes but Hare still had his basin. Hyena left the clothes and went to Hare's house for his basin.

Hare gave Hyena his large basin. He also gave Hyena a small basin.

Hare said, "Your basin gave birth to a young one and since we are friends, I am giving you the two of them." Hyena was happy and accepted the two basins.

blanks.why: 'Were great friends' needs a plural noun for the two animals.
'But' shows a contrast: both were poor, yet Hare owned a donkey.
'Used to' (for the purpose of) is followed by a base verb, and you feed an animal.
'Decided to give' is the past tense of 'decide to', matching the story.
'Could not' needs a base verb, and you 'fetch water' from a well.
You 'borrow' something 'from' someone; you 'lend' something 'to' someone.
'Because of' gives the reason: their friendship.
'Went home with' something means taking it along.

distractors: Hyena complained that he had been given more work.
One day they went to a river to drink water.
Hare agreed to his terms and they shook hands on it because he thought it was a good deal.
missing.why: Hyena needed his basin to wash clothes, so he went to Hare's house, and in the next sentence Hare gives the basin back.

highlights.question: Why did Hyena agree to lend his basin to Hare?
What did Hare claim had happened to Hyena's basin?

idea.answer: Hare returned Hyena's basin together with a small basin, saying it was the basin's baby.
distractors: Hyena refused to lend his basin because Hare never returned things.
Hare and Hyena stopped being friends after an argument about a basin.
Hare used Hyena's large basin to wash his own clothes at the river.
idea.why: Hare gave back the large basin and a small one, saying that Hyena's basin 'gave birth to a young one'.

distractors: Friendship between a donkey and a hyena
titles.why: The story is about Hyena and Hare and what happened to their basins.

interactive.title: Paradox 1: Culture Is Continuous, but It Changes
interactive.text:
Cultural materials, practices, and ideas are handed down from older to younger members of a culture, giving some degree of continuity to culture over time. However, many factors can intervene in this process of cultural reproduction to subtly alter or dramatically change the elements and aggregates of culture. In some contexts, younger people either fail to precisely learn the culture of their elders or deliberately reject those cultural lessons. Through travel and trade, people learn about other ways of doing things, and they take these ideas back to their own cultures, trying them out to see how they might improve their own ways of life. Accidents and deliberate experimentation introduce new possibilities. People may simply get tired of doing things one way over and over and thrill at some refreshing style or craze.

We can identify four main mechanisms of cultural change. These four mechanisms overlap and interact as the history of a culture unfolds over time. Diffusion is the movement of an element of culture from one society to another, often through migration or trade. Friction occurs when two or more elements of culture come into conflict, resulting in alteration or replacement of those elements.

blanks.why: 'Handed down' means passed from older people to younger people.
'However' introduces a contrast with the continuity described before.
'This process' refers back to handing culture down, which happens step by step.
'Either ... or' joins the two possibilities: fail to learn or reject.
'Elders' are older people, in contrast with 'younger people'.
'Through travel and trade' needs nouns for ways people meet other cultures.
We 'learn about' a topic, here other ways of doing things.
After 'might' we need a base verb; people try new ideas to improve their lives.

distractors: Cultural change can happen through invention or discovery.
New ideas, such as flash mobs or crowdfunding, enter a culture.
While it is an incredibly useful tool for understanding human social life, the concept of culture is riddled with paradox.
missing.why: The next sentence begins 'These four mechanisms', so the missing sentence must introduce the four mechanisms.

highlights.question: Why might people suddenly become excited about a new style or craze?
How does the passage define diffusion?

idea.answer: Although culture is passed down through generations, many things can cause it to change.
distractors: Culture never changes because young people always copy their elders exactly.
New technology such as smartphones is the main cause of cultural change.
Friction happens when two cultures agree to share their best ideas.
idea.why: The passage says culture is handed down, but many factors can alter or change it, and it names mechanisms of change.

titles.answer: Paradox 1: Culture Is Continuous, but It Changes
distractors: Paradox 4: Culture Is Shared, but It Varies
titles.why: The passage explains that culture continues over time but also keeps changing.

interactive.title: Birth Locations
interactive.text:
Many factors come in to play in the decision of where to give birth, including health insurance coverage, economic resources, the availability of nearby options, and existing health conditions or other considerations that may require special care. The question for the birth mother or future parents is, what is most important to them about the birth process.

About 98 percent of births in the United States occur in a hospital. In some parts of Europe and elsewhere around the world, birth more frequently occurs in a birthing center. One of the advantages of delivering in a hospital or birthing center is the ability to have vital signs like the heart rate and blood pressure continuously monitored. Changes in these can indicate distress or potential complications during the labor process, and medical interventions can be started quickly to ensure a safe delivery. More powerful medications are also available to assist with any discomfort during labor. Another benefit of institutional delivery is the series of automatic health screenings performed on newborns in hospitals and other medical settings.

blanks.why: 'The decision of where to ...' needs a noun after 'the'.
'The availability of' something is the usual pattern.
'Special care' is a common phrase; an adjective is needed before the noun 'care'.
'Future parents' are people who will soon become parents.
After the preposition 'to' we need the object pronoun 'them'.
After a number we use 'percent': 98 percent of births.
'Around the world' is a fixed phrase meaning in many places.
An adverb is needed to say how often birth occurs there.

distractors: This type of delivery can occur in multiple settings, including in a hospital, a birthing center, or at home, and depending on the location, in water.
Omar, on the other hand, expresses anxiety about this option and would feel safer with a hospital birth.
Low birth weight does not automatically result in developmental problems.
missing.why: 'Changes in these' refers to the vital signs in the sentence before and explains why watching them is an advantage.

highlights.question: What can be watched all the time during a delivery in a hospital or birthing center?
What is done for newborns in hospitals that is another advantage of delivering there?

idea.answer: Almost all babies in the United States are born in hospitals.
distractors: In most of Europe, nearly all babies are born at home without help.
Babies born in hospitals usually weigh more than babies born at home.
Health insurance does not affect where people choose to give birth.
idea.why: The passage says that about 98 percent of births in the United States occur in a hospital.

distractors: Care of Infants with Low Birth Weight
titles.why: The passage discusses where people give birth and the benefits of hospitals and birthing centers.

interactive.title: The Origin of Mercury
interactive.text:
The problem with understanding how Mercury formed is the reverse of the problem posed by the composition of the Moon. We have seen that, unlike the Moon, Mercury is composed mostly of metal. However, astronomers think that Mercury should have formed with roughly the same ratio of metal to silicate as that found on Earth or Venus. How did it lose so much of its rocky material?

The most probable explanation for Mercury’s silicate loss may be similar to the explanation for the Moon’s lack of a metal core. Mercury is likely to have experienced several giant impacts very early in its youth, and one or more of these may have torn away a fraction of its mantle and crust, leaving a body dominated by its iron core. A recent alternative explanation suggests that, early on, heat from the young Sun evaporated much of the lighter, more volatile, silicates in the material that formed Mercury, leaving the planet with a majority of metals.

blanks.why: 'How Mercury formed' needs a past-tense verb about how the planet came to exist.
'The reverse of' means the opposite of; a noun is needed after 'the'.
'Unlike the Moon' shows a difference between the two bodies.
'Composed mostly of' needs a noun naming a material; the passage then compares metal and silicate.
'Astronomers think that' means they believe something; a present-tense verb is needed.
'The same ... as' is the fixed pattern for saying two things are equal.
'Did it' is followed by the base verb 'lose'; 'loose' is an adjective.

distractors: It is the only planet known to have life on it.
This is very nearly the largest impact Earth could experience without being shattered.
Such an impact would disrupt much of Earth and eject a vast amount of material into space, releasing almost enough energy to break the planet apart.
missing.why: It begins to answer the question 'How did it lose so much of its rocky material?' and leads into the giant-impact explanation.

highlights.question: What might have removed part of Mercury's mantle and crust?
In the newer explanation, what caused much of Mercury's lighter silicates to evaporate?

idea.answer: Scientists have more than one possible explanation for why Mercury is mostly metal.
distractors: Mercury is made mostly of rock, just like Earth and Venus.
Mercury was formed from material thrown into space when a large object hit Earth.
Mercury's metal core grew larger because of heat from a nearby planet.
idea.why: The passage gives two explanations: giant impacts and heat from the young Sun.

titles.why: The whole passage is about how Mercury formed and why it is mostly metal.

interactive.title: Pliocene Hominins
interactive.text: Thirteen years after Raymond Dart’s discovery, South African paleontologist and medical doctor Robert Broom discovered Paranthropus robustus at a site called Kromdraai in South Africa. The most obvious difference between Dart’s and Broom’s respective fossils, A. africanus and P. robustus, is that the morphology of Broom’s fossil is much larger. Its features include a sagittal crest and a flared zygomatic arch for the attachment of a large temporalis muscle for chewing a diet reliant on hard nuts and seeds. This interpretation was further supported by scanning electron microscopy, which was used to evaluate the markings etched into the teeth. As the teeth increased in size the incisors and canines shrank, giving Paranthropus a flatter face with less projection of the jaw. There are some who argue that depending on the environment and locale, some Paranthropus may have been omnivores, with varied diets similar to those of H. ergaster..

blanks.why: 'Thirteen years after' an event places the second discovery later in time.
'Medical doctor' needs an adjective before 'doctor'.
A 'site' is a place where fossils are found; 'sight' means the ability to see.
'The difference between A and B' is used when comparing two things.
'Is that' introduces the clause that describes the difference.
'Much' is followed by a comparative such as 'larger' when two fossils are compared.
The plural subject 'features' needs the plural verb 'include'.
An adjective is needed before 'nuts and seeds', and big chewing muscles suit hard food.

distractors: The gracile species emerged around 4 MYA and disappeared 2 MYA, while robust species continued to exist for another million years.
Under most conditions, teeth and bones and impressions eventually deteriorate, too.
Sivapithecus fossils are very common throughout Asia, with a particularly large number having been found in Turkey.
missing.why: 'This interpretation' refers to the diet of hard nuts and seeds just described, and its mention of teeth leads into the next sentence.

highlights.question: Where did Robert Broom find Paranthropus robustus?
What happened to the front teeth as the other teeth became bigger?

idea.answer: Paranthropus robustus had strong chewing muscles suited to a diet of hard foods.
distractors: Paranthropus robustus had small teeth and ate mostly soft fruit.
Robert Broom found the first Paranthropus robustus fossil in Turkey.
Paranthropus robustus disappeared about four million years ago.
idea.why: The passage says its skull had places to attach a large chewing muscle for a diet of hard nuts and seeds.

distractors: Tools and Brains: Homo habilis, Homo ergaster, and Homo erectus
titles.why: The passage describes Paranthropus robustus, an early human relative (a hominin), not apes, monkeys or Homo species.

interactive.title: Focusing on Climate Change Solutions
interactive.text:
When it comes to climate change, we have the bad habit of focusing on the first part of the story, the part about the problem, and forgetting the second part about the many available solutions. These solutions are speeding up recycling, slowing down emissions and providing sustainable alternatives to plastic, air conditioning, smartphones and fast fashion.

The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recently gathered in Copenhagen to present its latest report on the impacts and pace of climate change. Climate change is now measured on all continents and our efforts to lower emissions must be intensified to avoid it escalating out of control. Along with outlining the risks and challenges, Copenhagen also embraced and focused on the solutions.

In the spirit of focusing on what can be done, Sustainia Award, chaired by Arnold Schwarzenegger, celebrated ten leading sustainability solutions deployed in 84 countries. From food to fashion, energy to transportation, education to health, the awards showcased an alternative to the grim-future scenarios we are so often presented with and made sustainability tangible to the innovators, investors, consumers and policy makers across sectors and regions.

blanks.why: 'When it comes to' is a fixed phrase meaning 'when we talk about'.
'The bad habit of doing something' means something we often do wrongly.
'Focusing ... and forgetting' are parallel -ing forms after 'habit of'.
'Speeding up' recycling contrasts with 'slowing down' emissions; both are -ing forms.
'Alternatives to' something is the usual pattern.
The possessive 'its' refers to the Panel's report; 'it's' means 'it is'.
'Is now measured' means at the present time.
'Out of control' is a fixed phrase meaning impossible to manage.

distractors: The increase in temperature causes climate change, which is a change in average worldwide or regional weather patterns.
This increase in greenhouse gases heats the earth.
Here are three of the key trends that experts predict will shape the transportation industry over the coming years.
missing.why: It moves from risks to solutions, which the next sentence continues with 'In the spirit of focusing on what can be done'.

highlights.question: Why did the climate change panel meet in Copenhagen?
What did the Sustainia Award celebrate?

idea.answer: People often talk about the problems of climate change but forget its many solutions.
distractors: Coal will soon replace oil as the world's biggest source of energy.
Reducing food waste is the most important way to stop climate change.
Climate change has so far been measured on only a few continents.
idea.why: The first sentence says we focus on the problem and forget the many available solutions.

distractors: Removing Harmful Greenhouse Gases from the Air Using Energy from Plants
titles.why: The passage is about paying attention to solutions to climate change, not only to its problems.

interactive.title: How to help someone in water
interactive.text: If someone is in water, you can use a stick to pull the person to safety. Never get into the water to try and rescue someone. If you get into the water, you could also drown. If the person who needs help is too far away from you to reach with a stick, you can throw something that floats. Throw something they can hold on to and use to stay above the water. You could throw a soccer ball or an empty five-litre plastic container. If someone needs rescuing from water, ask a lifeguard or adult for help. Never go into the water to try and rescue someone yourself. You can also call the free national emergency number, 112, from a cell phone or a landline. If someone is rescued from the water and they are not breathing, you should call 112 for help. You can then start Hands-on CPR by pushing hard and fast in the centre of their chest. Do not practice this on a friend! You can find out more from the National Sea Rescue Institute.

blanks.why: “Pull someone to safety” is a fixed phrase; after “to” here we need a noun, not the adjective “safe”.
“Get into the water” means to enter the water.
“Who” is the relative pronoun for a person, and here it is the subject of “needs”.
“Too far away” is the natural phrase for distance.
The object must stay on top of the water so the person can hold it; “something that” needs the verb “floats”.
“Hold on to” means to grip something and not let go.
To stay safe, the person must stay above the water, not under it.
A “soccer ball” is an object you can throw, and it floats.

distractors: The lifeguards on duty will put red and yellow flags on the beach to show you where it is safe to swim.
Many people find it hard to see a rip current in the sea.
This is why it is better to swim between the lifeguard flags.
missing.why: “Then” follows the advice to call 112, and the next sentence, “Do not practice this on a friend!”, needs “this” to mean Hands-on CPR.

highlights.question: Which floating objects does the passage suggest you could throw?
Who should you ask for help when a person needs to be rescued from water?

idea.answer: You should help a person in the water from a safe place instead of going into the water yourself.
distractors: It is safest to swim only at beaches where lifeguards are watching.
Strong swimmers should go into the water to help a person in trouble.
You should practise CPR on a friend so that you are ready for an emergency.
idea.why: The passage twice says never to go into the water and suggests using a stick or throwing something that floats.

titles.answer: How to help someone in water
distractors: The Bystander Effect and Diffusion of Responsibility
titles.why: The whole passage gives steps for helping someone who is in trouble in the water.

interactive.title: Agrobacterium: Nature's Genetic Engineer
interactive.text: Despite the many benefits of using Agrobacterium to improve crop plants, some groups seek to prevent the use of genetic engineering, and even try to misinform the public about the approach. One of the most common misunderstandings about genetic engineering is the belief that changing the DNA of an organism is unnatural and therefore wrong. However, Agrobacterium has been modifying the DNA of plants long before humans learned how to do it. This shows us that changing DNA sequences is a natural process and part of the world around us. By using Agrobacterium to modify plant DNA, we are harnessing a natural process to develop crop plants that need fewer pesticides, are more nutritious, and that yield more food using less land. Using less land is a really important consideration because, if we want to avoid the destruction of natural ecosystems, we need to make sure that our farms are as productive as possible. Genetically engineered crop plants can definitely help us to grow more food from less land, meaning that more ecosystems will be protected.

blanks.why: “Despite” needs a contrast: some groups oppose the method even though it has many benefits.
These groups oppose the method and even misinform people, so they want to stop (prevent) it; “seek to” needs a verb.
You inform or misinform people “about” a topic.
After “the” we need a noun, and a misunderstanding is a wrong belief, not a fact.
People think changing DNA is not natural, and that is why they call it “therefore wrong”.
“Has been modifying” is the present perfect continuous, and “Agrobacterium” is singular.
The point is that bacteria did this in nature first, long before humans could.

distractors: Transgenic plants have received DNA from other species.
An organism that receives the recombinant DNA is called a genetically modified organism.
Scientists are discovering how genomics can improve the quality and quantity of agricultural production.
missing.why: “This shows us” draws a conclusion from the sentence before, and its idea of a “natural process” is picked up in the next sentence.

highlights.question: What mistaken belief do many people have about genetic engineering?
Which three improvements in crop plants does the writer mention?

idea.answer: Using Agrobacterium to change crop DNA makes use of a natural process and can help protect natural ecosystems.
distractors: Thick plant cell walls make it harder to add DNA to plant cells than to animal cells.
Agrobacterium was first created by scientists working in a laboratory.
Genetically engineered crops need more land because they produce less food.
idea.why: The writer says Agrobacterium changes plant DNA naturally and that such crops grow more food on less land, so more ecosystems are protected.

titles.why: The passage explains how Agrobacterium moves its own genes into plants, which scientists now copy to engineer crops.

source.author: Johnathan J. Dalzell & Ryan T. Weir

interactive.title: Gene knockout
interactive.text:
A gene knockout is a genetic technique in which one of an organism's genes is switched off or replaced by one which does not work.

The organisms, such as knockout mice, are used to learn about a gene that has been sequenced, but whose function is unknown or incompletely known. Researchers draw inferences from the difference between the knockout organism and normal individuals. Knockout is often abbreviated as KO.

Gene knock-in is the opposite term. There a gene is switched on, or a working gene inserted.

Knockout is accomplished through a combination of techniques. It starts in the test tube with a plasmid, or other DNA construct, and proceeding to cell culture.

Individual cells are genetically transformed with the DNA construct. Often the goal is to create an animal that has the altered gene.

If so, embryonic stem cells are genetically transformed and inserted into early embryos. Resulting animals with the genetic change in their germline cells can then often pass the gene knockout to future generations.

blanks.why: “In which” starts a relative clause about a thing (a technique).
A knockout stops a gene from working, so the gene is switched off.
After “does not” we use the base verb, and a broken gene “does not work”.
“Such as” introduces an example (knockout mice).
“Are used to + base verb” gives the purpose: the organisms are used to learn about genes.
“But” and “or incompletely known” show that the gene’s function is not yet known.
After “the” we need a noun: researchers study the difference between the two groups.
Knock-in switches a gene on, the reverse of a knockout, so it is the opposite term.

distractors: The treatment by the product Glybera uses a virus to infect muscle cells with a working copy of the gene.
An organism that receives the recombinant DNA is called a genetically modified organism.
The total of all the genes in an organism is called the genome.
missing.why: It states the goal of transforming the cells, and the next sentence begins “If so”, which refers back to this goal of creating an animal.

highlights.question: Which two kinds of organisms do researchers compare to learn about a gene?
What type of cells is put into early embryos?

idea.answer: Scientists switch off a gene in an organism to find out what that gene does.
distractors: Gene knockout is used to give a working gene to people who have a damaged gene.
Animals with a gene knockout cannot pass the change on to their young.
Gene knock-in and gene knockout mean exactly the same thing.
idea.why: The passage says knockout organisms are used to learn about genes whose function is unknown by comparing them with normal individuals.

distractors: The Use of Stem Cells for Treatment of Diseases
titles.why: The whole passage explains what a gene knockout is, why it is used and how it is done.

interactive.title: All About Flamingos
interactive.text:
When you think of flamingos, you always remember their beautiful pink color. Amazingly, the birds get this color from the food they eat! Flamingos eat organisms such as plankton, shrimps, crabs and tiny water plants. All of these have special coloring agents which cause a flamingo to turn pink when it eats them.

If you take a flamingo away from its natural habitat and don't feed it these kinds of food, their color will turn whiter and whiter as days pass by. Flamingos are water birds – they live and feed near the sea coast and lakes as the food they eat is found in water. They are quite tall – some of them can grow up to a height of 1.5 meters. That is almost as tall as a human!

These birds have very long legs so they can walk far into the water. Although most photos will show you pictures of flamingos wading in the shallow water, these birds can also swim! Like other water birds such as ducks, flamingos have webbed feet. Webbed feet help birds push water back and swim across a water body.

blanks.why: We say “think of” something when it comes into our mind.
After “you always” we need a base verb, and a beautiful color is something you remember.
“The food they eat”: “they” (the birds) is the subject of “eat”.
Flamingos eat tiny living things found in water, including tiny water plants.
“Cause something to do” is the right pattern, and the subject “agents” is plural.
“Take something away from” a place is the fixed pattern.
A natural habitat is the place where an animal lives; a “habit” is something you do often.
“Whiter and whiter” repeats the comparative to show a color slowly changing.

distractors: They eat small crabs that live in the sand.
Elephants swim in rivers when they are hot.
They migrate, or travel from one place to live in another.
missing.why: It introduces webbed feet right after saying flamingos can swim, and the next sentence explains what webbed feet do.

highlights.question: What in their food turns flamingos pink?
Why do flamingos stay close to the sea and to lakes?

idea.answer: Flamingos are pink because of special colors in the food they eat.
distractors: Flamingos are born pink and keep the same color all their lives.
Flamingos cannot swim, so they only walk in shallow water.
Flamingos spend part of the year on warm beaches and part on the cold tundra.
idea.why: The passage explains that coloring agents in plankton, shrimps, crabs and water plants turn flamingos pink.

distractors: Why Didn’t the Bird Cross the Road?
titles.why: Every sentence describes flamingos: their colour, food, home, size, legs and feet.

source.title: The Dance of the Flamingo
source.author: Anita Mani
source.note: “The Dance of the Flamingo”, Anita Mani (freekidsbooks.org), CC BY 4.0; via the CommonLit CLEAR corpus

interactive.title: Searching for the Spirit of Celebration
interactive.text: Nkanyezi walked all day. She hiked up a hill, and down into a valley. She sailed across the great river, and climbed between sharp rocks. She marched across the plains until she reached the shadow of the red mountains. As night was closing in, Nkanyezi arrived at a village of patterns and colors as she had never seen before. She told the village elders about her journey to bring back the spirit of celebration to her people. The mother of this tribe gave Nkanyezi a gift. She told the girl, "With love we give to you this paint to restore color to your village." Nkanyezi thanked the elders and put the paint in her bag. Early the next morning she went on her way. Nkanyezi walked all day, through a vast forest of giant trees. As the sky became too dark for her to see, she heard the sound of beating drums. She hurried towards the drumming, feeling the spirit of dance coming to her tired feet.

blanks.why: You hike up “a hill”; after “a” the noun must be singular.
You sail across a river from one side to the other.
“Until” shows she kept marching up to the moment she reached the mountains.
We say “arrive at” a place; “reached” and “entered” take no “at”.
“As she had never seen before” means the village was new to her.
We “tell someone about something”; “said”, “spoke” and “talked” cannot take “the village elders” as an object.
After “the spirit of” we need a noun, and she wants to bring joy back, not sadness.
“Tribe” is singular, so it needs “this”.

distractors: Drums enrich songs and make people want to dance.
One Wednesday afternoon, the ten boys went to the forest to search for snails.
The giant asked the girl loved by both parents to help her carry firewood.
missing.why: The next sentence says she hurried “towards the drumming”, so the drums must be heard just before it.

highlights.question: What was the purpose of Nkanyezi’s journey?
What was the paint meant to do?

idea.answer: On her journey, Nkanyezi was given paint to bring color back to her village.
distractors: Nkanyezi stayed in the colorful village for many weeks.
The village elders refused to help Nkanyezi on her journey.
Nkanyezi went into the forest with ten boys to look for snails.
idea.why: The mother of the tribe gives Nkanyezi paint “to restore color to your village”.

titles.answer: Searching for the Spirit of Celebration
titles.why: The story follows Nkanyezi's journey to bring back the spirit of celebration.

source.author: Mosa Mahlaba

interactive.title: Lion gets sick
interactive.text:
One day, all the wild animals got together to choose a king.

They saw that it would be good to choose Lion to be the king of the animals.

At that meeting, they crowned Lion the king of the animals. As part of the ceremony, they had a big party that lasted a week.

All of the animals attended the ceremony until the end. They ate, they drank, they sang and they danced.

When the ceremony was over, they all dispersed. They were returning to their homes.

It was the custom for every animal to go and greet Lion because he was their king.

One visitor who came to greet King Lion was Hyena. When Hyena arrived at Lion's house, he found the king in bed.

Lion told him, "I'm sick with an incurable illness."

Hyena responded, "O, Great King, don't be sad because of your illness. Hare knows the cure for this illness."

blanks.why: “Get together” means to meet as a group.
Before “be” we need a modal verb: “it would be good”.
“At that meeting” refers back to the animals getting together; “that” needs a singular noun.
“As part of” is a fixed phrase meaning “included in”.
The party went on for a week, so it “lasted” a week (past tense).
“Attend a ceremony” means to be there; “went” and “arrived” would need “to” or “at”.
“Until the end” means they stayed up to the last moment.
“Was over” means had finished.

distractors: Hyena complained that he had been given more work.
Hyena suggested that it was good to plant maize.
Hyena believes in working hard and not getting things for free.
missing.why: Hyena arrives and finds Lion in bed, which explains why Lion then tells “him” that he is sick.

highlights.question: According to the custom, why did every animal go to greet Lion?
What good news does Hyena give Lion?

idea.answer: When Hyena visited King Lion, he found that Lion was ill.
distractors: The animals chose Hyena to be their king.
Hare and Hyena were great friends who did many things together.
Only a few animals stayed at the ceremony until it ended.
idea.why: Hyena comes to greet King Lion and finds him in bed, sick with an illness.

distractors: Sheep who got tired of city life
titles.why: The story leads up to the new king, Lion, falling ill.

source.author: Francisco Escondido

interactive.title: Anansi and wisdom
interactive.text: One day, Nyame decided that he would give the pot of wisdom to Anansi. Every time Anansi looked in the clay pot, he learned something new. It was so exciting! Greedy Anansi thought, "I'll keep the pot safe at the top of a tall tree. Then I can have it all to myself!" He spun a long thread, wound it round the clay pot, and tied it to his stomach. He began to climb the tree. But it was hard climbing the tree with the pot bumping him in the knees all the time. All the time Anansi's young son had been standing at the bottom of the tree watching. He said, "Wouldn't it be easier to climb if you tied the pot to your back instead?" Anansi tried tying the clay pot full of wisdom to his back, and it really was a lot easier. In no time he reached the top of the tree. But then he stopped and thought, "I'm supposed to be the one with all the wisdom, and here my son was cleverer than me!" Anansi was so angry about this that he threw the clay pot down out of the tree.

blanks.why: Looking into the pot of wisdom taught him things, so he “learned” something new (past tense).
Use “exciting” for the thing that causes the feeling; “excited” describes how a person feels.
Anansi is speaking about himself, so the phrase is “have it all to myself”.
Spiders spin a thread, and “a” needs a singular noun.
The pot is tied to Anansi’s own stomach, so the possessive “his” is needed.
“Began” is the past tense of “begin”; “begun” needs “has” or “had”.
“But” and the pot hitting his knees show the climb was difficult; “hardly” means “almost not”.
“With the pot bumping him” describes what was happening during the climb.

distractors: Let me tie one end of this web around my leg and one end to your pot.
Then, Anansi felt a pull on one of his legs.
Quietly, Fati started to climb the mango tree.
missing.why: The son speaks after watching, and Anansi’s next action, tying the pot to his back, follows the son’s idea.

highlights.question: Where did Anansi plan to keep the pot safe?
Where was Anansi’s son while his father was climbing?

idea.answer: Anansi’s son showed him an easier way to carry the pot up the tree.
distractors: Anansi shared the pot of wisdom with everyone in his village.
Anansi’s son climbed the tree and took the pot for himself.
Nyame kept all the stories locked in a wooden box high in the sky.
idea.why: The son suggests tying the pot to his back, and Anansi finds that it really is easier.

titles.why: The whole story is about Anansi and the pot of wisdom, and how his son proves wiser than him.

interactive.title: The Bystander Effect and Diffusion of Responsibility
interactive.text:
Social psychologists have recognized that other people’s presence influences our behavior, whether we are aware of it or not. One example is the bystander effect, a situation in which people are less likely to interfere during an emergency or when a social norm is being violated if there are others around. They feel less responsible because of the presence of other bystanders. This is known as diffusion of responsibility.

Most of the time people report that they don’t want to get involved and that’s why they don’t respond when they see something wrong. They assume someone else will step up and help. Researchers have found that people are less likely to help if they don’t know the victim.

Think about it this way, you’re walking to class and there are several students around. Someone falls on the ground having a seizure. What would you do? The bystander effect suggests that unless you know the person who has fallen, you are more likely to walk away than help. However, social psychologists believe that you are much more likely to help, or at least stop and check, if you are the only one around.

blanks.why: The subject “presence” is singular, so the verb is “influences”.
“Whether … or not” means “in either case”.
“One example is” introduces a case of the general idea.
“Less likely to do something” means less probable to do it.
“Others” is a pronoun meaning other people; “other” needs a noun after it.
“Is known as” gives the name of something; we say “is called diffusion…” without “as”.
“Get involved” means to take part in a situation.
“Someone else” means a different person.

distractors: Researchers have used scenarios such as this to understand social cognition in children.
Situationism is the view that our behavior and actions are determined by our immediate environment and surroundings.
Children with a negative bias, or hostile attributional error, are more likely to interpret the friend’s behavior as an aggressive or purposefully unkind act.
missing.why: It answers “What would you do?”, and the next sentence’s “However” contrasts with walking away instead of helping.

highlights.question: What makes people feel less responsible in an emergency?
When are you likely to help even a stranger, according to social psychologists?

idea.answer: People are less likely to help in an emergency when other people are present.
distractors: Children often see a friend’s unfriendly behavior as an aggressive act.
People are more likely to help a stranger than someone they know.
Our behavior is decided only by our personality, not by the situation.
idea.why: The passage explains the bystander effect: people step in less often when others are around.

titles.answer: The Bystander Effect and Diffusion of Responsibility
distractors: Interpreting and Responding to Social Situations
What Is Epilepsy and How Can You Help Someone With It?
titles.why: The whole passage explains the bystander effect and why people feel less responsible when others are present.

source.title: The Bystander Effect and Diffusion of Responsibility
source.note: “The Bystander Effect and Diffusion of Responsibility”, Introduction to Sociology 3e, OpenStax (Rice University), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

interactive.title: Peopling Mesoamerica
interactive.text: To the south and west of the Eastern Woodlands, the climate is much more arid and less green. This desert scrubland extends down the center of Mexico to the tip of the Central Mexican Plateau. South of there, in the region often described as Mesoamerica, the environment is warmer, greener, and wetter. The formerly large-game-hunting peoples settled there after around 8000 BCE as the game disappeared and the bison followed the retreating grassland north. Evidence of Archaic peoples in this area has been found in several coastal sites along the Gulf of Mexico and the Pacific Ocean, as well as in the Tehuacán Valley south of modern Mexico City. They lived largely in small groups and hunted and gathered over large areas. During the dry season, they relied mostly on wild game like lizards, snakes, and insects, and edible plants like the agave. During the rainy season, they ate avocados, nuts, various types of fruit, and small game, like rabbits.

blanks.why: “Much” makes a comparative stronger: “much more arid”.
“Less” goes with adjectives (“less green”); “fewer” goes with plural nouns.
The singular subject “scrubland” needs the present-tense verb “extends”.
We say “described as”; “called” is used without “as”.
It matches the other comparatives, “greener, and wetter”, which contrast with the dry land to the north.
“Settled there” means settled in that place (Mesoamerica).
The peoples were only “formerly” big-game hunters because the large animals disappeared.
The bison moved north after the grassland, so they “followed” it (past tense).

distractors: Hunting bison was dangerous and required keeping a distance in order to not startle the animals or allow them to grow reflexively fearful of human presence.
In addition to bison, the plains peoples also hunted antelope, deer, and small animals like rabbits and birds.
In Mesoamerica it was squash and later maize, or corn, and in China millet and rice.
missing.why: It gives the foods of the dry season, which pairs with the next sentence about the rainy season.

highlights.question: What was happening to the large game and the bison when the hunters settled in Mesoamerica?
What did the Archaic peoples eat in the wet part of the year?

idea.answer: The Archaic peoples of Mesoamerica ate different foods in the dry season and the rainy season.
distractors: The Archaic peoples of Mesoamerica lived in large cities and grew maize.
Mesoamerica is drier and less green than the land to its north.
The bison adapted to the warmer climate and stayed in Mesoamerica.
idea.why: The passage lists lizards, snakes, insects and agave for the dry season, and avocados, nuts and fruit for the rainy season.

titles.why: The passage describes the land of Mesoamerica and the first peoples who settled and lived there.

source.title: Peopling Mesoamerica
source.note: “Peopling Mesoamerica”, World History, Volume 1, OpenStax (Rice University), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

interactive.title: Speciation through Geographic Separation
interactive.text: A geographically continuous population has a gene pool that is relatively homogeneous. Gene flow, the movement of alleles across the range of the species, is relatively free because individuals can move and then mate with individuals in their new location. Thus, the frequency of an allele at one end of a distribution will be similar to the frequency of the allele at the other end. When populations become geographically discontinuous that free-flow of alleles is prevented. When that separation lasts for a period of time, the two populations are able to evolve along different trajectories. Thus, their allele frequencies at numerous genetic loci gradually become more and more different as new alleles independently arise by mutation in each population. Typically, environmental conditions, such as climate, resources, predators, and competitors, for the two populations will differ causing natural selection to favor divergent adaptations in each group. Different histories of genetic drift, enhanced because the populations are smaller than the parent population, will also lead to divergence.

blanks.why: A singular subject (“population”) takes “has”.
“Gene pool” is the fixed term for all the genes in a population.
After “the” we need a noun: gene flow is the movement of alleles.
Gene flow is easy (“free”) because individuals can move; an adjective follows “is relatively”.
“Their” is the possessive for “individuals”.
“Similar to” is the right pattern, and free gene flow keeps the two ends alike.
“At one end … at the other end” is a fixed pair.
When populations are separated, gene flow is stopped: “is prevented” (passive).

distractors: A mutation can change one allele into another, but the net effect is a change in frequency.
In population genetic terms, evolution is defined as a change in the frequency of an allele in a population.
Gorillas, for example, cannot successfully breed with Pan paniscus, the bonobo.
missing.why: “That separation” refers back to the populations becoming separated, and “the two populations” is what “their” refers to in the next sentence.

highlights.question: How does the passage define gene flow?
Which environmental conditions may differ for the two populations?

idea.answer: When two populations are separated for a long time, their genes slowly become more and more different.
distractors: Genetic drift has the strongest effect in very large populations.
Separated populations keep the same allele frequencies because new mutations stop appearing.
In a continuous population, an allele is usually far more common at one end of the range than at the other.
idea.why: The passage explains that separation stops gene flow, so the two populations evolve along different paths.

titles.why: The whole passage explains how geographic separation makes two populations grow genetically different.

source.title: Speciation through Geographic Separation
source.note: “Speciation through Geographic Separation”, Concepts of Biology, OpenStax (Rice University), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

interactive.title: Industrial Society
interactive.text:
In the eighteenth century, Europe experienced a dramatic rise in technological invention, ushering in an era known as the Industrial Revolution. What made this period remarkable was the number of new inventions that influenced people’s daily lives. Within a generation, tasks that had until this point required months of labor became achievable in a matter of days. Before the Industrial Revolution, work was largely person- or animal-based, and relied on human workers or horses to power mills and drive pumps. In 1782, James Watt and Matthew Boulton created a steam engine that could do the work of twelve horses by itself.

Steam power began appearing everywhere. Instead of paying artisans to painstakingly spin wool and weave it into cloth, people turned to textile mills that produced fabric quickly at a better price and often with better quality. Rather than planting and harvesting fields by hand, farmers were able to purchase mechanical seeders and threshing machines that caused agricultural productivity to soar. Products such as paper and glass became available to the average person, and the quality and accessibility of education and health care soared. Gas lights allowed increased visibility in the dark, and towns and cities developed a nightlife.

blanks.why: “A rise in” something means an increase, and the Industrial Revolution came from more invention, not less.
“Made this period” needs an adjective, and so many inventions made it special.
Use “number” with countable nouns like “inventions”; “amount” is for uncountable nouns.
“Within a generation” means in less time than one generation.
Tasks that took months became possible in days, which shows a great speed-up.
“In a matter of days” is a fixed phrase meaning in only a few days.
The verb “rely” is always followed by “on”.
Before steam, people and horses powered the mills; the plural noun is needed after “or”.
“By itself” means alone, without help; “engine” is singular and not a person.

distractors: This could move a pump directly or work a crank to turn a wheel and work a machine.
It had also begun to enter a new phase of development.
By the late 1800s, the Industrial Revolution had spread beyond Great Britain.
missing.why: Like the sentence before it (“Instead of paying artisans…”), it shows work once done by hand being done by machines, this time on farms.

highlights.question: How much work could Watt and Boulton’s steam engine do on its own?
Which products could the average person now get?

idea.answer: New machines in the Industrial Revolution made many everyday tasks much faster.
distractors: The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain and later spread to the United States.
Most people still paid artisans to spin wool and weave cloth by hand.
Machines made goods faster, but the goods were of lower quality than before.
idea.why: The passage says tasks that took months could be done in days, and it lists machines that changed daily life.

titles.why: The passage describes how new machines changed work and daily life as society became industrial.

source.title: Industrial Society
source.note: “Industrial Society”, Introduction to Sociology 3e, OpenStax (Rice University), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

interactive.title: Fitness
interactive.text:
Not many exercise classes have a tea break in the middle. But Margaret Allen’s class has one. After a gentle warm-up and a few quick exercises, the 93-year-old great-grandmother lets her group sit down and relax with a cup of tea. Some of the eight people in the class look like they need a break, but Allen is not even sweating.

The general rule is that eating just before doing sport is not a good idea and especially not halfway through the class. But, on the afternoon I visit Allen’s class in Saltburn-by-the-Sea, they eat fruitcake during the break. The cake was made for Allen’s recent birthday by her 89-year-old sister, Joan.

The ladies have just finished their cake when Allen gets up again. She plays a lively Scottish song and there is lots of toe pointing and leg kicking. Forty-five minutes later, the class is finally over.

blanks.why: “Many” goes with plural countable nouns like “classes”.
A “tea break” is a short rest for a cup of tea; a “brake” stops a car.
“A few” is used with plural countable nouns like “exercises”.
“Let someone do something” takes a base verb with no “to”.
After “lets her group sit down and” we need a base verb, like “sit”.
“Is not even sweating” is the present continuous, and it contrasts with the people who need a break.
We say “do sport”, and after “before” we use the -ing form.
“Halfway through” means in the middle of an activity.

distractors: But after six weeks they saw the results and were surprised.
He saw that short bursts of very hard exercise were as effective as hours of normal exercise.
Performances at school sports days in the weeks ahead may bear out the findings.
missing.why: “But” contrasts with the rule against eating, and “fruitcake” prepares for “The cake was made…” in the next sentence.

highlights.question: What drink does Allen’s group have during the break?
Who baked the fruitcake for Allen’s birthday?

idea.answer: At the age of 93, Margaret Allen still leads a lively exercise class.
distractors: Allen’s students are not allowed to eat anything during the class.
Short bursts of very hard exercise work as well as hours of normal exercise.
Allen gets tired quickly and needs the tea break more than her students.
idea.why: The writer describes the 93-year-old leading warm-ups, exercises and a lively dance without even sweating.

titles.why: The passage is about staying fit through an exercise class, even at 93.

source.title: Fitness
source.note: “Fitness” (elementary version), OneStopEnglish corpus (Vajjala & Lučić, 2018), CC BY-SA 4.0

interactive.title: Stem Cells in the Human Body
interactive.text:
Our bodies are made up of trillions of small units, known as cells. However, at the very early phase of development, we were embryos consisting of only a tiny clump of cells. Cells in an embryo are in a primitive state, and we call them embryonic stem cells. Embryonic stem cells can develop into three types of cells, called ectodermal stem cells, endodermal stem cells, and mesodermal stem cells. These three types of stem cells then go on to form 200 different types of cells. For example, stem cells form the cells of your skin, the red blood cells in your blood, and the cells that produce the color of your eyes. Altogether, stem cells form all the organs and tissues in the body, such as the bones, kidneys, liver, blood, and brain. After birth, embryonic stem cells are no longer present in the body.

However, even in the bodies of children, adults, and elderly people, we find several types of stem cells. These stem cells can form some, but not all, of the 200 different cell types.

blanks.why: 'Be made up of' is a fixed phrase that means 'consist of'.
After 'phase of' we need a noun, and an embryo is the first stage of a person's development.
'Consisting of' means 'made of'; 'containing' and 'including' are not followed by 'of'.
'Embryo' is a singular noun that starts with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'.
'We call them X' means 'we give them the name X'; the other verbs cannot be used this way.
'Develop into' means 'grow and change until it becomes'.
'Three types' is plural and points back to the types just named, so it needs 'These'.
'Go on to' is followed by a base verb, and stem cells form (make) other cells.

distractors: Ongoing cell differentiation allows cells to become specialized to do different jobs.
The empty egg is then injected with DNA from another mature cell, such as a skin or blood cell.
This cell divides mitotically to produce a multicellular organism.
missing.why: It says embryonic stem cells disappear after birth, which the next sentence contrasts with 'However, even in the bodies of children, adults...'.

highlights.question: Which groups of people still have some types of stem cells in their bodies?
How many types of cells do the three types of stem cells go on to form?

idea.answer: Stem cells can turn into the many different kinds of cells that make up the body's organs and tissues.
distractors: Doctors can treat brain injuries by putting new stem cells into the patient's body.
Embryonic stem cells stay in the body for the whole of a person's life.
The stem cells found in adults can form every one of the 200 cell types.
idea.why: The passage says stem cells form about 200 types of cells and all the organs and tissues of the body.

titles.answer: Stem Cells in the Human Body
distractors: Making Neurons from Human Stem Cells
titles.why: The whole passage explains what stem cells are and how they form the cells of the body, from the embryo to old age.

source.title: The Use of Stem Cells for Treatment of Diseases
source.author: Franka Luk, Elke Eggenhofer, Marc H. Dahlke, and Martin J. Hoogduijn
source.note: “The Use of Stem Cells for Treatment of Diseases”, Franka Luk, Elke Eggenhofer, Marc H. Dahlke, and Martin J. Hoogduijn (kids.frontiersin.org), CC BY 4.0; via the CommonLit CLEAR corpus

interactive.title: Overclocking
interactive.text: Overclocking is the process of configuring a computer processor or other electronic circuit to run faster than it was designed to. Overclocking allows a computer to be faster and more responsive. Overclocked processors tend to use more electricity and make more heat than those running at their intended speed. It is often necessary to install a better heat sink to avoid overheating the processor. If a processor is overclocked too high, it can damage the processor or make the computer unstable. Increasing the voltage to the processor can allow it to be run at even higher speeds where it would otherwise be unstable, but this carries an especially high risk of damaging the processor. Overclocking is usually done in the computer's BIOS setup utility. Most brand-name computers such as Dell, HP, and others do not allow overclocking in the BIOS setup utility, but custom-built computers usually do. It is also possible to do the opposite, called underclocking, where the processor is run at a lower speed than intended. This may be done to extend battery life and reduce heat output. Underclocking will not usually damage a processor and may in fact make it last longer.

blanks.why: A comparative like 'faster' is followed by 'than'.
'Allow something to do' is correct; 'let' and 'make' are followed by a verb without 'to'.
After 'use more' we need a noun for the power a processor uses: electricity.
A possessive word is needed before 'intended speed'; 'their' refers to 'those' processors.
After 'to' we need a base verb, and a heat sink is used to avoid (stop) overheating.
'Too high' means 'more than is safe', which explains the damage in the rest of the sentence.
'Make something + adjective': a computer that does not work reliably is unstable.
'A high risk of damaging' is a common phrase for a strong chance of harm.

distractors: Usually, the contents of RAM are accessible faster than other types of information storage but are lost every time the computer is turned off.
Intel Core processors are based on Pentium M technology.
Software is any set of machine-readable instructions that directs a computer's processor to perform specific operations.
missing.why: It introduces the BIOS setup utility, which the next sentence refers back to when it says brand-name computers do not allow overclocking there.

highlights.question: Why might someone choose to run a processor at a lower speed?
What may need to be fitted to stop an overclocked processor from getting too hot?

idea.answer: Making a processor run faster than intended can speed up a computer, but it also creates more heat and risk.
distractors: Information in a computer's memory is lost every time the computer is turned off.
Most brand-name computers make overclocking easy to do in their setup utility.
Underclocking is risky because it often damages the processor.
idea.why: The passage says overclocking makes a computer faster and more responsive but uses more electricity, makes more heat and can damage the processor.

titles.why: Almost every sentence is about overclocking: what it is, its benefits and risks, where it is done, and its opposite.
